messages:
hana: FYI we just got an elevated support ticket from FinSight — p95/p99 spike on /v1/generate after yesterday's continuous-batcher tuning. Ticket INC-8274. Can SRE please triage?

alex: thanks. Do we have the exact batcher config they rolled (hold/window/max_batch_size)? Also which model and region?

hana: pasted the config they changed:
```json
{
  "batcher_mode": "continuous",
  "hold_window_ms": 20,
  "max_batch_size": 64,
  "grace_window_ms": 5
}
```
They were on redwood/gpt-open-13b, us-west-2. Customer says spike started ~2026-03-15T02:12Z. We repro'd in staging with a traffic replay (mixed tiny prompts) and saw p99 up ~450ms from baseline 120ms.

raj: that config change rings a bell. Increasing hold_window is expected to raise throughput but for tiny/mixed workloads it can increase tail latencies when bursts contain many tiny reqs that get coalesced and then suffer KV cache thrash. Did they also change max_batch_bytes or the greedy coalesce flag?

hana: only changed the three fields above. No other flags. We attached a short replay script we ran:
```bash
# replay tiny/mixed load to staging
python replay.py --tenant finsight --mix tiny:0.8 medium:0.2 --rps 200 --duration 10m
```
Logs show a pattern: many batches formed with size 40-60 but a subset (~3%) waited close to 18-19ms and then runtime queued them into a large batch causing token scheduling stalls.

alex: can you paste the excerpt of the runtime trace (request ids) where a batch waited and then p99 jumped? need x-request-id traces + kernel-latencies. Also mark the sample spans for kv-cache misses.

hana: sample trace snippet:
```
x-request-id=fin-3ab1e
batch_size=58 hold_ms=19.2 schedule_wait=0.9 gpu_exec_ms=320 kv_cache_miss=12
```
and another:
```
x-request-id=fin-3ab7b
batch_size=12 hold_ms=1.1 gpu_exec_ms=48 kv_cache_miss=0
```
Shows big variance.

raj: yep. High batch_size + big model causes skew: a bunch of tiny prompts grouped with a few long ones. Suggested quick mitigations (apply as tenant-level policy):
- reduce hold_window_ms to 8ms
- cap max_batch_size to 24 for the tenant
- enable small_request_bypass: true (bypass batching for payloads < 512 bytes)
- enable batcher_dynamic_grace=true (so small bursts don't wait for big ones)
These can be toggled via the admin API or console.

alex: agree. Also request pprof traces from the GPU nodes during replay, and enable runtime debug=coalesce for 15m so we capture queue histograms. We should also snapshot model kernels selection at time of spike.

hana: rolling the quick changes now to the tenant policy (will keep them live for 30m then revert if stable). Applying via admin API:
```http
POST /admin/tenants/finsight/policy
{ "hold_window_ms": 8, "max_batch_size": 24, "small_request_bypass": true }
```

deploy-bot: Started rollout 61823 for tenant finsight: policy-update -> servers: rtx-pool-usw2-1..3 (canary 10%)

hana: monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/obs/tenants/finsight/queries?p95,p99,tail (pls keep an eye)

michelle: any auth/billing fallout from the policy change? a customer mentioned earlier that billing seemed to spike last week.

hana: not from this policy change; this is purely batching timing. I confirmed billing meter counts unchanged in the last hour.

ops-bot: Alert: tenant finsight p99 > 400ms (rule: tenant-tail-p99). Triggered 2026-03-15T02:19Z.

alex: good. After the canary, if p99 drops to baseline, we can push cluster-wide for that tenant. If not, fallback plan B is to temporarily route finsight to dedicated reserved capacity (dedicated pool) until they adjust their client to avoid mixing tiny+long prompts.

raj: also log a follow-up: consider adding an autosuggestion in Console when hold_window > 10ms to warn for tiny-payload-heavy tenants. Could save other teams.

hana: canary finished, metrics look improved: p95 down from 310ms -> 140ms, p99 down from 480ms -> 160ms within 6 minutes of change. I put a note on INC-8274 and asked FinSight to keep us posted.

alex: excellent. Please collect the debug logs (coalesce histograms + GPU pprof) for the 30m window and upload to the ticket. We'll draft a short postmortem recommending conservative defaults for hold_window and a Console warning.

hana: uploaded logs to INC-8274 and added replay artifacts + commands to reproduce. I'll follow up with the customer with a summary and next steps (recommend client-side batching hints + tenant policy).

michelle: thanks team. Tagging @oncall for visibility.

alex: moving to close this Slack thread — we'll open a lightweight postmortem doc in #postmortems if needed.

hana: closing here, will ping when PM/pm follow-up is done. :white_check_mark:
